scope: Local codec ownership diagnostic; mutations deliberately violate the current immutable-geometry convention
method: Encode a project containing two different entities whose distinct coordinate arrays have equal values, and a history entry referring to both entities; decode it and mutate the first restored array.

observed.ordinaryArray: Both entities received the same array; mutation through one was visible through the other.
observed.float32Array: Both entities received the same typed array; mutation through one was visible through the other.
observed.historyAlias: The history entry retained the intended alias to its corresponding current entity.

cause: The encoder deduplicates chunks by content hash and the decoder caches values by chunk and type, so distinct equal source arrays are not distinguished by this format path.

regression.status: expected failure for independent mutable ownership

limitations: The test uses direct in-memory mutations, not a demonstrated GUI or MCP operation.
No binary-format or decoder change is included; legacy-file compatibility, intended history aliases and memory limits require a coherent design.
Float64 restore remains experimental and M2 remains open.
